scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

podcast.title: Death Details - May 7, 2024
podcast.body: Steve Albini died on May 7th, 2024, at the age of 61, from a heart attack at his home. "Steve died of a heart attack at his home on May 7th, the age of 61."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Analog Recording Techniques
podcast.body: He favored analog recording technology, consciously avoided overdubbing whenever possible, and minimized the use of outboard effects, resulting in raw and authentic recordings. "He preferred analog technology. He avoided overdubbing where possible, and he kept outboard effects to the bare minimum, and the results were raw, authentic recordings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Artists Produced by Albini
podcast.body: Steve Albini has worked with a diverse array of artists, including The Stooges, The Jesus Lizard, Mogwai, Fugazi, Joanna Newsom, Superchunk, and Coil. These collaborations showcase his wide-ranging influence and consistent application of his distinctive production style across various genres. "Ha trabajado con destuges, de armyscoker, Monkwife, Fugaci, Slim, Johanna Newsome, Super Choo, Colo, y vamos a analizar siete de los mejores y más importantes discos de su carrera como productor."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Birth and Early Musical Influence
podcast.body: Born in 1962 in Pasadena, Steve Albini's musical journey began after he heard The Ramones' album *Wut*. This experience prompted him to buy a bass guitar and subsequently play in various punk bands throughout his adolescence. "Nacido en 1962 en Pasadena al Vinitra, se escuchar el disco de Wut de los Ramones se compró un bajo y toco varias bandas de pongo durante la asociencia."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Career Philosophy: Challenging Conventions
podcast.body: Throughout his career, Steve Albini has actively challenged musical conventions, consistently operating against prevailing trends. He firmly adheres to his core musical principles: a minimalist, analog, and homemade approach, coupled with an unwavering devotion to sonic honesty. These principles are deemed more critical today than ever, in a world where music increasingly becomes compressed, equalized, and uniform. "Este falbínia, a lo largo de su carrera, ha deshacado las convenciones musicales a leer a contra corriente, acerándose siempre a sus principios musicales, son foques minimalistas, analógico y casero, y su devoción por la unistiraz sonora, son más importantes hoy que nunca en un mundo que está volviendo ese cada vez más comprimido, más equalizado y más uniforme."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Champion Poker Player
podcast.body: Steve Albini, renowned as a producer for bands like Nirvana and the Pixies, is also a champion poker player. He was taught to play by his great-grandmother as a child and won his first World Series of Poker Title in a seven-card stud tournament in Las Vegas, beating 30 other players and taking home $106,000. "And earlier this year, he beat 30 other players to win his first World Series of Poker Title, taking a part of $106,000 in a seven-card stud tournament in Las Vegas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

podcast.title: Critique of Modern Production Trends
podcast.body: Steve Albini asserts that 99% of contemporary music sounds identical, a phenomenon he attributes to producers' pervasive obsession with excessive compression and equalization. He views these practices as detrimental to sonic diversity and integrity. "Afirma que el 99% de la música son igual y con los productores están obsesionados con la compresión y la cualización."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Dislike of "Producer" Title and Arrangements
podcast.body: Steve Albini dislikes being referred to as a "producer" and never involves himself in musical arrangements. He sees his role as a technical engineer, focused solely on capturing a band's sound rather than shaping its artistic direction. "No le gusta que le llame un productor y además nunca hace arreglos."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Engineer for Iconic Albums
podcast.body: Albini engineered several highly acclaimed albums, including Pixies' "Surfer Rosa" (1988), The Breeders' "Pod" (1990), PJ Harvey's "Rid of Me," and most notably, Nirvana's "In Utero," playing a crucial role in its sound. "Steve Elbeany was a very big part of the sound of Inuro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Extensive Client List
podcast.body: His clients spanned a long list of intense indie bands, but also included more mainstream acts such as Bush (for "Razorblade Suitcase"), Cheap Trick, The Sadies, The Stooges, Scott Weiland, Manic Street Preachers, and Canada's Metz. "His other clients included a long list of intense indie bands, but also Bush for Rook Assault, Cheap Trick, the Sadie's Pez, the band that would become Billy Town. The Stuges, Scott W island, Manic Street Preatures, and Canada's Metz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Flat Rate Payment Model
podcast.body: Unlike most producers who take a percentage of royalties, Albini charged a flat fee for his services. For example, he could have earned millions from Nirvana's "In Utero" but reportedly only requested $100,000, choosing to forego backend royalties. "He could have made millions from just Inudero, but all he really wanted was, I think, $100,000. And that's it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Formation of Big Black
podcast.body: Steve Albini formed his band Big Black in 1981, marking an early milestone in his career where he began experimenting with his distinctive production approach. "En 1981 formó Big Black."

srcs.source: Central Sonora

podcast.title: Formation of Rapeman
podcast.body: Steve Albini formed the band Rapeman in 1997. "En 1997 Reimen."

srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Formation of Shellac
podcast.body: Steve Albini formed Shellac in 1992, and the band remains active. This project has allowed him to continue exploring his unique recording and performance philosophies. "en 1992 Shalak, con los que siguen activo."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Guitarist in Chicago Bands
podcast.body: Steve Albini was a guitarist in several Chicago-based bands, including Big Black and Rapeman. "Steve was a guitarist in a variety of Chicago bands, Big Black, Ray Man, and a few others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Last Project - Kim Deal Solo Record
podcast.body: The last record Steve Albini was involved with was Kim Deal's solo record, "Nobody Loves You More," which was released in 2024 and critically acclaimed as one of the year's best alt-rock albums. "And the last record he was part of was the excellent Kim Deal solo record, Nobody Loves You More, which was one of the very best alt rock albums of 2024."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Minimal Effects and Preservation of Imperfections
podcast.body: In his recordings, Steve Albini favors using few effects and intentionally retains errors made by musicians during sessions. This approach underscores his commitment to natural sound and authentic performance, avoiding over-polished production. "De gusta usar pocos efectos en las grabaciones y dejar errores que tengan los músicos durante las sesiones."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Obsession with Raw Sound
podcast.body: Albini's strong desire to capture the raw and direct sound of rock music led him to experiment extensively with production techniques, particularly within his own bands. This obsession has been a defining characteristic of his work throughout his career. "Su obsesión por capturar la crudeza del sonido más directo del rock le hizo experimentar con la producción de sus bandas."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: One-Week Recording Philosophy
podcast.body: Albini adheres to a philosophy that an album can be recorded in approximately one week. He believes this timeframe is crucial for capturing the immediacy of the initial takes, which he feels best preserve the spirit and energy of live concerts. "Sus tiene que son la rota de armas de una semana en grabar un disco, ya que es parte de adió de la inmediatez de las primeras tomas, las cuales son las que mejor recogen el espíritu de los conciertos."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Refusal of Royalties
podcast.body: Distinct from many other producers, Steve Albini consistently refuses to accept royalties for the music he records. He prefers to be paid a flat fee for his engineering work, rather than benefiting from the ongoing sales of the music he helps create. "Se nega recibe regalías por la música que raba, a diferencia de cómo hacía en otros productores."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Self-Perception as a "Plumber"
podcast.body: In contrast to "guru" producers like Rick Rubin, Steve Albini views himself more as a "plumber" who simply performs his job and is compensated for his technical skill. This analogy highlights his pragmatic and unpretentious approach to his craft, as he famously articulated in a letter sent to Kurt Cobain. "él se percibe más como un fontanero que hace su trabajo y le pagan lo que vale, como aferse una carta enviada a Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Specialization in Live Recording
podcast.body: Steve Albini is renowned for his expertise in recording bands live, a practice that he notes is becoming increasingly rare in modern music production. This method is central to his philosophy of capturing authentic performances. "Es un especialista en grabar a las bandas en directo, cosa que cada vez es más rara."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: 7 discos para entender la producción de STEVE ALBINI

podcast.title: Street Named in Chicago
podcast.body: A road in Chicago, where his studio Electrical Audio is located, has been named "Steve Albini Way" in his honor. "Finally, if you're ever in Chicago, the road where his studio, Electrical Audio, is now called Steve Elbeniway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Uncredited Work with Urge Overkill
podcast.body: He also contributed to Urge Overkill's "Super Sonic Storybook" without receiving official credit. "He's uncredited with fellow Chicagoans, urge overkill on Super Sonic Storybook."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam 2024

podcast.title: Unique Recording Philosophy
podcast.body: Albini was known for his distinct philosophy in the studio, which focused on capturing the authentic essence of an artist's sound rather than acting as a traditional "producer." He considered himself more of a recording engineer. "His philosophy was to capture the essence of an artist's sound in the studio."

xref.title: Steve Albini's Master Tapes Hostage Situation
xref.body: Producer Steve Albini had a deal stipulating no changes after his final mix. When the label wanted modifications to *In Utero*, he refused to hand over the master tapes, "essentially holding them hostage," until bassist Chris Novoselic convinced him to comply. "He even refused to hand over the master tapes for a while, essentially holding them hostage."

xref.title: Support from Indie Musicians
xref.body: Indie musicians in Chicago and beyond, including producer Steve Albini and a former bandmate of Billy Corgan from a pre-Smashing Pumpkins band, took notice and supported Wesley. The Canadian industrial metal band Monster Voodoo Machine recorded with him, and Eddie Vedder was charmed by his work. "The indie musicians of Chicago and beyond took note, and they took a liking to him."
